Two fixes fit here: default to cgroupfs, or make `cmd_selfcheck` fail closed while the daemon runs in systemd mode.
  confidence=5

  EVIDENCE: `VALIDATION_HARNESS_SANDBOX_CGROUP_MODE` still defaults to `auto`. `start_rootless_dockerd` (lines 363-372) still starts the rootless daemon under the sandbox user's systemd user manager (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=${runtime_dir}/bus`), and `DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_FLAGS=--pidns` does not close the route. `sandbox_start_verified_dockerd` keeps systemd mode when it is available (lines 473-484). The launcher masks manager sockets only in the harness's own mount namespace (lines 261-279), so a container started through the rootless daemon can bind-mount the unmasked `/run/user/<uid>/systemd/private`, reach the manager, and start a process outside the harness PID namespace. `selfcheck` still reports ok. The changelog fragment changelog.d/7349-validation-harness-pid-namespace.md and the agents.d fragment both document this residual: "A container started through Docker can still reach that manager in this mode and list runner processes and their command lines". The only mitigation is a manual operator setting, `VALIDATION_HARNESS_SANDBOX_CGROUP_MODE=cgroupfs`. No diff hunk changes the default or adds a fail-closed check. The deferral (TASK_GAP_DEFERRED) came from the editor round, not from the issue. The narrower `/proc/<pid>/environ` credential exposure is closed.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

Not repeating gemini's `docker.sock` point, because a replacement breaks `rootless_docker_ready` in `cmd_run` (line 924) and the run fails closed. No other categories had findings.
